problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 3 \\ -1 & 2 & -2\end{aligned}],\,B={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c \\ d\end{aligned}]}
$$

Consider the subspace $V=\text{Col}(A)$ spanned by the columns ${a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}$ of the matrix $A$ and an orthogonal basis $B$ of $\text{Col}(A),$ shown above. Given that ${a}_{1}⊥{a}_{2},$ and that $B$ is derived from $V$ using the Gram-Schmidt process, what is the value of $\frac{c}{b}?$

Consider the subspace $V=\textrm{Col}(A)$ spanned by the columns $\mathbf{a}_1,\mathbf{a}_2,\mathbf{a}_3$ of the matrix $A,$ and an **orthonormal** basis $\mathcal{B}$ of $\textrm{Col}(A),$ shown above. Given that $\mathbf{a}_1 \perp \mathbf{a}_2,$ and that $\mathcal B$ is derived from $V$ using the Gram-Schmidt process, what is the value of $|\,d\,|?$
examples.worked_solution:
Since the first two vectors are already orthogonal, we proceed to find an orthogonal basis using the Gram-Schmidt process.

**Step 1**: We set ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14072057/assets/fac944c1f224d01dc33db95a5971ff47483e04ecf06492d8cfecb44d05de225c.png)

**Step 2**: We set ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14072057/assets/ce3195325db5c00042ec58cb51b8e17c77df742112ea7ad6481920647a6c77bb.png)

**Step 3**. Next, we find $\mathbf{v}_3$ using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{3} & ={a}_{3}-{\text{proj}}_{{v}_{1}}\,{a}_{3}-{\text{proj}}_{{v}_{2}}\,{a}_{3} \\  & ={a}_{3}-\frac{{a}_{3}\cdot {v}_{1}}{{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}}{v}_{1}-\frac{{a}_{3}\cdot {v}_{2}}{{v}_{2}\cdot {v}_{2}}{v}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the formula for $\mathbf{v}_3$ in our case gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{3} & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 6 \\ 0\end{aligned}]-\frac{10}{10}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-\frac{20}{20}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 6 \\ 0\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -2 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we normalize $\mathbf{v}_3$ dividing it by $\|\mathbf{v}_3\| = \sqrt{10}\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{3} & =\frac{{v}_{3}}{‖{v}_{3}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -2 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{\sqrt{10}}{10} \\ -\frac{\sqrt{10}}{5} \\ \frac{\sqrt{10}}{5} \\ -\frac{\sqrt{10}}{10}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, $|\,d\,| = \left|-\dfrac{\sqrt{10}}{10}\right|=\dfrac{\sqrt{10}}{10}.$

feedback.problem:
$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -3 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,B={[\begin{aligned}| \\ \frac{{a}_{1}}{‖{a}_{1}‖} \\ |\end{aligned}]\,,[\begin{aligned}| \\ \frac{{a}_{2}}{‖{a}_{2}‖} \\ |\end{aligned}]\,,[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c \\ d\end{aligned}]}
$$

Suppose that $V=\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}.$ Given that $B$ is an **orthonormal** basis for $V,{a}_{1}⊥{a}_{2},$ and that $B$ is derived from $V$ using the Gram-Schmidt process, what is the value of $|\,c\,|?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since the first two vectors are already orthogonal, we proceed to find an orthogonal basis using the Gram-Schmidt process, as follows:

**Step 1**: We set ${v}_{1}={a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$

**Step 2**: We set ${v}_{2}={a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -3 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$

**Step 3**. Next, we find ${v}_{3}$ using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{3} & ={a}_{3}-{\text{proj}}_{{v}_{1}}\,{a}_{3}-{\text{proj}}_{{v}_{2}}\,{a}_{3} \\  & ={a}_{3}-\frac{{a}_{3}\cdot {v}_{1}}{{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}}{v}_{1}-\frac{{a}_{3}\cdot {v}_{2}}{{v}_{2}\cdot {v}_{2}}{v}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the formula for ${v}_{3}$ in our case gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{3} & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-(-\frac{4}{4})[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]-(-\frac{8}{12})[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -3 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+\frac{2}{3}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -3 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(3[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+3[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+2[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -3 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we normalize ${v}_{3}$ dividing it by $‖{v}_{3}‖=\frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{3} & =\frac{{v}_{3}}{‖{v}_{3}‖}=\frac{1}{(\frac{\sqrt{6}}{3})}\cdot \frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{\sqrt{6}}{6} \\ 0 \\ \frac{\sqrt{6}}{3} \\ \frac{\sqrt{6}}{6}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, $|\,c\,|=\frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}.$
